Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: The one element of the stroke Paul had tried to remember was the one thing he didn’t do! Everything else had been absorbed and reproduced without a word being uttered or an instruction being given!

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: images are better than words, showing better than telling, too much instruction worse than none, and that trying often produces negative results.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Quieting the mind means less thinking, calculating, judging, worrying, fearing, hoping, trying, regretting, controlling, jittering or distracting.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: First the mind judges the event, then groups events, then identifies with the combined event and finally judges itself.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: In the Chinese tradition of medicine, patients visit their doctors when they are well and the doctor is expected to keep them well. It would be equally possible, and much less frustrating, to approach the tennis pro with your backhand just the way it is without the judgment.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: it. If he hits the balls out, I will notice they go out, and I may notice the reason why they are going out. But is there a need to judge him or the backhand as sick? If I do, I am likely to get as uptight in the process of correcting him as he is likely to be in correcting himself. Judgment

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: you should realize the importance of being aware of where the racket head is at all times. You can’t look at it to know where it is because you’re watching the ball. You must feel it. Feeling it gives you the knowledge of where it is. Knowing where it should be isn’t feeling where it is. Knowing what your racket didn’t do isn’t feeling where it is. Feeling where it is is knowing where it is.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Uncomfortable without a standard for right and wrong, the judgmental mind makes up standards of its own. Meanwhile, attention is taken off what is and placed on the process of trying to do things right.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: It is impossible to judge one event as positive without seeing other events as not positive or as negative.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Often when we are rallying we trust our bodies and let it happen because the ego-mind tells itself that it doesn’t really count. But once the game begins, watch Self 1 take over; at the crucial point it starts to doubt whether Self 2 will perform well.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Getting the clearest possible image of your desired outcomes is a most useful method for communicating with Self 2, especially when playing a match.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: I have found that when players break their habitual patterns, they can greatly extend the limits of their own style and explore subdued aspects of their personality.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: As either teacher or student we will be most ourselves and most effective only to the extent that we can be in harmony with it.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: if we hit the ball relying on the instincts of Self 2, we reinforce the simplest neural pathway to the optimal shot.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: The more awareness one can bring to bear on any action, the more feedback one gets from experience, and the more naturally one learns the technique that feels best and works best for any given player at any given state of development.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: And many of us have lost touch with feel. We may need to learn how to feel again and learn how to learn again.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Before beginning, let me simplify the external requirements of tennis. The player has only two requirements for success: hit each ball over the net and into the court.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: The same goes for how tightly you should grip the racket. Just try to describe this in language! My best effort at this was borrowed from a fencing instruction given to Cyrano de Bergerac: “Hold the foil as a bird, not so loosely that it can fly away, but not so tightly that you squeeze the life out of it.”

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: This first step of knowing what results you want is critical to maintaining control of the learning process where it belongs—with you.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: By the word “learning” I do not mean the collection of information, but the realization of something which actually changes one’s behavior—either external behavior, such as a tennis stroke, or internal behavior, such as a pattern of thought. We all develop characteristic patterns of acting and thinking, and each such pattern exists because it serves a function.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: If you think you are controlled by a bad habit, then you will feel you have to try to break it. A child doesn’t have to break the habit of crawling, because he doesn’t think he has a habit. He simply leaves it as he finds walking an easier way to get around.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Awareness of what is, without judgment, is relaxing, and is the best precondition for change.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: The focused mind only picks up on those aspects of a situation that are needed to accomplish the task at hand. It is not distracted by other thoughts or external events, it is totally engrossed in whatever is relevant in the here and now.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Distraction is then like dirt on the lens of the light or like the light jerking around so quickly that illumination is effectively reduced.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Broad focus would be an attempt to see as much of the forest at one time as possible. Narrow focus would be directing attention to something very specific like the veins on a particular leaf on a particular twig of a branch.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Self 2, may be the only thing which has been there and will be there your entire life. Thoughts and thinking come and go, but the child self, the true self, is there and will be there as long as our breath is. To enjoy it, to appreciate it, is the gift of focus.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Regardless of whether he is watching the game at a country club, a public park or a private court, he will see players suffering everything from minor frustration to major exasperation. He will see the stomping of feet, shaking of fists, war dances, rituals, pleas, oaths and prayers; rackets are thrown against fences in anger, into the air for joy, or pounded against the concrete in disgust. Balls that are in will be called out, and vice versa. Linesmen are threatened, ball boys scolded and the integrity of friends questioned.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Do we really think the value of a human being is measurable? It doesn’t really make sense to measure ourselves in comparison with other immeasurable beings. In fact, we are what we are; we are not how well we happen to perform at a given moment. The grade on a report card may measure an ability in arithmetic, but it doesn’t measure the person’s value. Similarly, the score of a tennis match may be an indication of how well I performed or how hard I tried, but it does not define me, nor give me cause to consider myself as something more or less than I was before the match.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: The surfer waits for the big wave because he values the challenge it presents. He values the obstacles the wave puts between him and his goal of riding the wave to the beach. Why? Because it is those very obstacles, the size and churning power of the wave, which draw from the surfer his greatest effort. It is only against the big waves that he is required to use all his skill, all his courage and concentration to overcome; only then can he realize the true limits of his capacities.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Each player tries his hardest to defeat the other, but in this use of competition it isn’t the other person we are defeating; it is simply a matter of overcoming the obstacles he presents. In true competition no person is defeated. Both players benefit by their efforts to overcome the obstacles presented by the other.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: You don’t have to become a killer to be a winner; you merely have to realize that killing is not the name of the game.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Today I play every point to win. It’s simple and it’s good. I don’t worry about winning or losing the match, but whether or not I am making the maximum effort during every point because I realize that that is where the true value lies.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: “When it comes to overcoming obstacles, there are three kinds of people. The first kind sees most obstacles as insurmountable and walks away. The second kind sees an obstacle and says, I can overcome it, and starts to dig under, climb over, or blast through it. The third type of person, before deciding to overcome the obstacle, tries to find a viewpoint where what is on the other side of the obstacle can be seen. Then, only if the reward is worth the effort, does he attempt to overcome the obstacle.”

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Perhaps the most indispensable tool for human beings in modern times is the ability to remain calm in the midst of rapid and unsettling changes.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: Inner stability is achieved not by burying one’s head in the sand at the sight of danger, but by acquiring the ability to see the true nature of what is happening and to respond appropriately.

Title: The Inner Game of Tennis: The Classic Guide to the Mental Side of Peak Performance
Author: W. Timothy Gallwey, Pete Carroll, Bill Gates, and Zach Kleiman
Highlight Text: takes as much trust to fully focus attention when listening to another person without carrying on a side conversation in your own head as it does to watch a tennis ball in all its detail, without listening to Self 1’s worries, hopes and instructions.

Title: The Island
Author: Adrian McKinty
Highlight Text: “Well, Danny?” she asked. “No one will ever replace Ellen, but it’s better than nothing,” he said. “Life’s a balance. Nature treated you harshly today. This restores the balance. You can take her,” Ma said.

Title: The Island
Author: Adrian McKinty
Highlight Text: Your body is a longbow carved from hickory, her father said. Your body is a blade sharpened by tears, her mother said.

Title: The Island
Author: Adrian McKinty
Highlight Text: “I am Trouble with a capital T. I’m Death with a capital D. If you give me any problems at all, I won’t hesitate to kill you. Do you understand?”

Title: The Island
Author: Adrian McKinty
Highlight Text: She knew if he pulled the trigger, she wouldn’t feel a thing. She wouldn’t hear anything. Her life would instantly cut to black. The blackness would last until the end of the universe, when everything would be black.

Title: The Island
Author: Adrian McKinty
Highlight Text: There were no monsters on Dutch Island, but the beast was man, had always been man.

Title: The Island
Author: Adrian McKinty
Highlight Text: A black iron nothingness. An ellipsis of time. Perhaps a minute; perhaps ten thousand million years. A nimbus of yellow goblin light.

Title: The Island
Author: Adrian McKinty
Highlight Text: It was night, and the barbarians were coming. The only question was whether the barbarians were them or her.

Title: The Island
Author: Adrian McKinty
Highlight Text: She squeezed the trigger, and the rifle thumped comfortingly into her right shoulder. The explosive in the cartridge threw out a lead ogive that the barrel spiraled into the air with the faintest rush of smoke and the sweet smell of gunpowder. The bullet had been on a collision course with its target since it was manufactured in North London in 1941.

Title: The Island
Author: Adrian McKinty
Highlight Text: You know what she is, Matthew? She’s the monster. The bunyip. She’ll destroy us unless we destroy her. We got to get her.”

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: I made a decision that while cancer may define how I die, it would not define how I live.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: The journey of The Last Arrow begins when you raise the bar. We need to raise the bar of our standards of our faith, of our sacrifice, of our expectations of ourselves, of our belief of the goodness and generosity of God.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: I wonder how many times in my own life I thought I failed but actually the only thing that happened was that I quit.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Wouldn’t it be better for all of us if we were incapable of knowing that there’s more? How often is our greatest torment, that haunting thought, that the lives we long to live are not the lives we were created to live?

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Maybe those of us most aware of our imperfections and flaws are best suited for this journey. After all, what do we have to lose? We were never supposed to amount to anything. If failure is our inevitable future, then let’s fail boldly and fail forward.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: But the moments that will actually define us, the moments that will carry the greatest weight in our lives, the moments that will create for us the future we’ve always longed for, are not those moments that easily integrate into our past, but instead they are the disruptive moments, the moments when we must choose between extending our past and creating our future.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: If slavery remains an option, we will find ourselves abdicating our freedom. We just don’t usually call it slavery. We call it safety. We call it comfort. We call it security. We call it responsibility.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: It’s not that those who settle for less don’t want more for their lives; it’s that they want the “more” where they are and are not willing to go where the “more” is waiting for them. Yet over and over again, we find that God presses against us and forces us to choose.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: We are afraid that if we leave something behind in our past, there is not something better waiting for us in the future.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Sometimes, though, it’s not the people who keep us in the past; it’s our own sense of identity.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: There is a subtle difference between your identity being rooted in your essence and your identity being rooted in your success. What you do comes out of who you are, but who you are must exist apart from what you do.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Success is a tyrant that will enslave you just as quickly as failure. If you let success own you, you will find yourself trapped by your success and terrified by the possibility of failure.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: If those trophies are the highlights of our lives, then our lives were not worth living, going forward. Those trophies were the past, and it would be a waste of our time and effort to try to reclaim the past. It would be much better for us to focus on creating the future.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Setting your past on fire is not about self-destructive behavior. In fact, it is quite the opposite. It is about making the hard decisions to leave behind that which would steal from you the future God intends for you.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: It’s more important to get where you are going than to take what you brought with you.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Refuse to stay behind. Never ever opt out of the opportunities that move you in the direction of your dreams, your purpose, your passions.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: People who are constantly praying about everything may be doing too much talking and not enough listening. The point of prayer is response. And once God has spoken, you don’t need to pray about that anymore—unless, of course, you are trying to change his mind.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Life is cruel in this: if you are willing to be left behind, the future will leave you in the past and opportunity will depart.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: When God tells you to strike an arrow, you just keep striking and striking and striking and you do not stop until you hear heaven shout, “It is finished.”

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Don’t wait to be asked—volunteer. Volunteer to go forward. Volunteer to go further. Volunteer to go harder. You cannot pioneer out of obligation. It is not an adventure if it is not your choice. You have to want it. You have to want more. If you are going to be greedy, this is the right place to be greedy. Want everything God has for you. Want more than others think you can obtain. Why settle for a single portion if a double portion can be yours for the asking?

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: cannot ensure how long I live, but I can determine that I will live fully while I’m alive.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Too many of us act as if we’re going to live forever or that life can wait until we’re ready to live it. But when it comes to life, we get no trial runs. We get no practice games. And when it comes to life, you need to act as though your life depends on it.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: For Shammah, there is no point in running for your life if once you get there you have no reason to live.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: All of us, whether consciously or unconsciously, find a piece of ground where we choose to take our stand. Yet the reality is that for far too many of us, the place where we set our feet is rarely the result of a decisive decision to stop running and start fighting.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: How strange that there are people in this world who have taken more care to decide where they will die than how they will live.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: We think that life is either a sprint or a marathon but that in either case we are the only runner who matters. If life is a race, it is far more like a relay in which we do not win if we do not have a team that will help us get across the finish line.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: we are more powerful when we walk together, and we are more vulnerable when we walk alone.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: How you end is profoundly affected by how you begin. You never begin the journey of creating the life you want until you know what you want. It’s only when you know what you want that you can say no to everything that wants you.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: If you don’t know what you want, then God’s trying to give you what he wants for you is a wasted effort. You have to want what God wants in order to receive what he wants to give you.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: If we choose to live a small life, we do not make enough room for a big God.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: If you don’t know what you want, you will get what you do not want. If you don’t know who you want to become, you will become someone you never wanted to be. If you don’t know what life you want to live, you’re going to live the life someone else wants you to live. If you don’t know what you want God to do in your life, you will wonder why he gave you so little, while the whole time he was waiting for you to see how much he wanted to entrust with you.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Be faithful in the small things that do not matter to you as much and treat them with the same level of respect and importance as the big things connected to your hopes and dreams.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: it is the person who is faithful in the small things who will be entrusted with bigger things.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: “When the body touched Elisha’s bones,” we’re told, “the man came to life and stood up on his feet.”3 I think this is a not-so-subtle reminder that if you truly live before you die, your life will have a power that not even death can conquer.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Though it was a tragic death, there’s something strangely beautiful about that moment: being able to whisper with your last breath one word that lets the world know you did exactly what you were born to do. In that moment, death has no power, death has no victory. There is no regret—only a deep sense of fulfillment.

Title: The Last Arrow: Save Nothing for the Next Life
Author: Erwin Raphael McManus
Highlight Text: Ralph Waldo Emerson said, “The way to write is to throw your body at the mark when your arrows are spent.”6 I agree wholeheartedly, except I would add one particular nuance: that the way to live is to throw your body at the mark when your arrows are spent.

Title: The Last Pirate of New York: A Ghost Ship, a Killer, and the Birth of a Gangster Nation
Author: Rich Cohen
Highlight Text: Even in the last moment, when you have nothing ahead but a swinging rope, you still have the possibility of escape.

Title: The Last Pirate of New York: A Ghost Ship, a Killer, and the Birth of a Gangster Nation
Author: Rich Cohen
Highlight Text: To a Freemason, the world is an allegory shot through with symbols and signs meant to lead the faithful toward enlightenment. These hints are complicated and interlocked, like wheels within wheels, set in place by a hidden power. To Hicks, it would have suggested the existence of at least two worlds: one where things were as they appeared, and another where all the usual meanings were inverted. In that second world, the criminal was the hero and the condemned man was king.

Title: The Last Pirate of New York: A Ghost Ship, a Killer, and the Birth of a Gangster Nation
Author: Rich Cohen
Highlight Text: Oh, to that precombustion age, when you could plan and plan but nature would decide! Oh, to those still afternoons and evenings when sailors stood on the decks of great ships, whistling for the wind as the sun set over New Jersey, amid the evening sounds, the sea hawk and the night owl.

Title: The Last Pirate of New York: A Ghost Ship, a Killer, and the Birth of a Gangster Nation
Author: Rich Cohen
Highlight Text: At the end of the search, you find yourself puzzled. You are expecting a monster, but you find only a man. Or maybe it’s something more. Maybe you are expecting God or the devil, or an answer to a fundamental question, and instead you discover yourself in a small room in a small city as a child cries.

Title: The Last Pirate of New York: A Ghost Ship, a Killer, and the Birth of a Gangster Nation
Author: Rich Cohen
Highlight Text: It was Barnum who created the Times Square energy, the spectacle and the con that, other than the Bill of Rights, is about all we have left of old America. The movies and vast entertainment zones, Disney World and Las Vegas, Spider-Man, rock ’n’ roll, our current politics—it all grew out of P. T. Barnum’s original insight: believing is seeing.

Title: The Last Pirate of New York: A Ghost Ship, a Killer, and the Birth of a Gangster Nation
Author: Rich Cohen
Highlight Text: She opened the locket and removed the picture. Behind it were a few locks from Oliver’s head. “I cut his hair,” she explained. “I did it once a month. It grew so quickly.” The strands were given to the jurors, who examined them next to some hair found in the blood on the deck of the sloop. This side-by-side study was about as close as you got to forensic analysis in 1860. The hair apparently came from the same person. Asked her opinion, Miss Dickerson said, “It’s indeed from Oliver. I knew every hair on his head. I knew it better than he knew it himself.”

Title: The Last Pirate of New York: A Ghost Ship, a Killer, and the Birth of a Gangster Nation
Author: Rich Cohen
Highlight Text: The camps were isolated, a half-day ride from help, protected by an idiot with a rifle. There were no cops, no soldiers. The land was lawless—no order other than what you imposed. It was an ideal setup for desperadoes, a buffet, a smorgasbord. They could go in, take what they wanted, then head back for more.

Title: The Last Pirate of New York: A Ghost Ship, a Killer, and the Birth of a Gangster Nation
Author: Rich Cohen
Highlight Text: In a heartbeat, it had gone from nothing to everything, from a small Spanish mission and fort called Yerba Buena to a wild metropolis annexed by the United States and renamed for its picturesque bay. Between 1846 and 1850, 200 inhabitants became 21,000. It was less a city than a stampede, a delirium. It can feel like that still, cresting and falling on great floods of commerce: beat poets, hippies, computer programmers. It’s insubstantial as a result, pumped up, phony. From a distance, it’s a picture on a soap bubble—towers, bridges, sea. You hold your breath, waiting for it to pop.

Title: The Last Pirate of New York: A Ghost Ship, a Killer, and the Birth of a Gangster Nation
Author: Rich Cohen
Highlight Text: New Orleans entered the Union as part of the Louisiana Purchase. It was a focal point in the War of 1812. In the Battle of New Orleans, fought after the war itself had ended—as usual, the city was late—General Andrew Jackson joined with the pirate Jean Lafitte to beat back the British. In other words, New Orleans was kind of a pirate city.

Title: The Last Pirate of New York: A Ghost Ship, a Killer, and the Birth of a Gangster Nation
Author: Rich Cohen
Highlight Text: What did Hicks have inside? At times, it seemed like he had nothing inside, just appetite and anger, a simple drive to avenge whatever slight he believed he’d suffered. At other times, as when he rescued the cabin boy from whipping, you sensed there was something, that his was a soul in torment, trapped and deformed, battling its own nature.

Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: The point is this: The way we think toward our jobs determines how our subordinates think toward their jobs.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Practice uplifting self-praise. Don’t practice belittling self-punishment. You are what you think you are. Think more of yourself and there is more of you.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Here’s how to build your “sell-yourself-to-yourself” commercial. First, select your assets, your points of superiority. Ask yourself, “What are my best qualities?” Don’t be shy in describing yourself.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Don’t accept the judgment of average people. You are not average. If you have any doubts as to the basic soundness of the “sell-yourself-to-yourself” principle, ask the most successful person you know what he thinks about it. Ask him, and then start selling yourself to yourself.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Remember: People who tell you it cannot be done almost always are unsuccessful people, are strictly average or mediocre at best in terms of accomplishment. The opinions of these people can be poison.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 1. Do circulate in new groups. Restricting your social environment to the same small group produces boredom, dullness, dissatisfaction; equally important, remember that your success-building program requires that you become an expert in understanding people.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 2. Do select friends who have views different from your own. In this modern age, the narrow individual hasn’t much future.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 3. Do select friends who stand above petty, unimportant things. Folks who are more concerned with the square footage of your home or the appliances you have or don’t have than with your ideas and your conversation are inclined to be petty.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Taking an ax and chopping your neighbor’s furniture to pieces won’t make your furniture look one bit better; and using verbal axes and grenades on another person doesn’t do one thing to make you a better you or me a better me.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Of course, I’ve heard the argument many times “but I can’t afford to go first class.” The simplest answer is: you cannot afford to go any other way.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Develop an instinct for quality. It pays. And it costs no more, often costs less, than second class.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 1. Grow the attitude of I’m activated. 2. Grow the attitude of You are important. 3. Grow the attitude of Service first.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: To activate others, to get them to be enthusiastic, you must first be enthusiastic yourself.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: A man who lacks enthusiasm never develops it in another. But a person who is enthusiastic soon has enthusiastic followers.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 1. Dig into it deeper.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Use the dig-into-it-deeper technique to develop enthusiasm toward other people.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: There’s one way to build enthusiasm toward a new location. Simply resolve to dig into the new community. Learn all you can about it. Mix with the people.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Just dig in deeper and you dig up interest.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Life up your talk. Dr. James F. Bender, the noted speech authority, in his excellent book How to Talk Well, says, “Is your ‘Good morning!’ really good? Are your ‘Congratulations!’ enthusiastic? Does your ‘How are you?’ sound interested? When you make a habit of coloring your words with sincere feelings you’ll notice a great uptake in your ability to hold attention.”

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Transmit good news to your family. Tell them the good that happened today. Recall the amusing, pleasant things you experienced and let the unpleasant things stay buried. Spread good news. It’s pointless to pass on the bad.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: They take hot weather in stride until the negative news corps educate them to be conscious of unpleasant temperatures. Make it a habit always to speak favorably about the weather regardless of what the weather actually is. Complaining about the weather makes you more miserable and it spreads misery to others.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Transmit good news to the people you work with. Give them encouragement, compliment them at every opportunity. Tell them about the positive things the company is doing. Listen to their problems. Be helpful. Encourage people and win their support. Pat them on the back for the job they’re doing.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: “Give me a Good Word or none at all.”

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: This is a fact of paramount significance: Each human being, whether he lives in India or Indianapolis, whether he’s ignorant or brilliant, civilized or uncivilized, young or old, has this desire: He wants to feel important.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Satisfying the craving, the hunger, to be important carries you forward to success. It is basic equipment in your success tool chest.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: It’s not too wild a guess that, of all living creatures, probably not more than one in ten million is a human being. A person is a biological rarity. He is important in God’s scheme of things.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: It pays to make “little” people feel like big people. Today, in thousands of offices all over America, secretaries are helping salesmen make sales or lose sales depending on how the salesman has treated them. Make someone feel important, and he cares about you. And when he cares about you, he does more for you.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: It pays to make “big” people feel even bigger. The big thinker always adds value to people by visualizing them at their best. Because he thinks big about people, he gets their best out of them.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Let’s not kid ourselves. People who do not have a deep-down feeling of self-importance are slated for mediocrity.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: You must feel important to succeed. Helping others to feel important rewards you because it makes you feel more important.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 1. Practice appreciation. Make it a rule to let others know you appreciate what they do for you. Never, never let anyone feel he is taken for granted.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 2. Practice calling people by their names.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 3. Don’t hog glory, invest it instead.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: WANT TO MAKE MONEY? THEN GET THE PUT-SERVICE-FIRST ATTITUDE

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: And the seed of money is service. That’s why “put service first” is an attitude that creates wealth. Put service first, and money takes care of itself.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Put service first, and money takes care of itself—always.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: But this is not how the system works. You don’t get a raise on the promise of better performance; you get a raise only by demonstrating better performance.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: But the get-rich-quick producer seldom does get rich quick. There never is a bandwagon movement to buy anything second-class, especially when it is given a first-class price.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Always give people more than they expect to get. Each little extra something you do for others is a money seed. Volunteering to work late and get the department out of a tight spot is a money seed; giving customers extra service is a money seed because it brings customers back; advancing a new idea that will increase efficiency is a money seed.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: The answer, wrapped up in one phrase, is think right toward people. Think right toward people, and they will like and support you. This chapter shows how.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Mark this point well. A person is not pulled up to a higher-level job. Rather, he is lifted up. In this day and age nobody has time or patience to pull another up the job ladder, degree by painful degree. The individual is chosen whose record makes him stand higher than the rest.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: But don’t try to buy friendship; it’s not for sale. Giving gifts is a wonderful practice if the gift is backed up with genuine sincerity, a liking to give and liking for the person to whom it is given. But without real sincerity, the gift is often regarded as nothing more than a payoff or a bribe.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Yes, it’s easy and natural, but it isn’t right thinking toward people. If you follow the rule of letting the other person build the foundation for friendship, you may not have many friends.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 2. Recognize the fact that the other fellow has a right to be different. Never play God about anything. Never dislike people because their habits are different from your own or because they prefer different

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Substitute the word employees for customers so that it reads “employees should be treated like guests in my home.” Give first-class treatment to your employees, and you get first-class cooperation, first-class output. Think first class about everyone around you, and you’ll receive first-class results in return.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Here’s how you can have some fun and discover a basic success principle at the same time. For the next two days listen in on as many conversations as you can. Note two things: which person in the conversation does the most talking and which person is the more successful.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Remember this: the average person would rather talk about himself than anything else in this world. When you give him the chance, he likes you for it. Conversation generosity is the easiest, simplest, and surest way there is to win a friend.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 1. Ask yourself, “What can I do to make myself more deserving of the next opportunity?” 2. Don’t waste time and energy being discouraged. Don’t berate yourself. Plan to win next time.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 7. Don’t blame others when you receive a setback. Remember, how you think when you lose determines how long it will be until you win.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: As one executive explained, there are many almost-qualified people, but there is one success ingredient often missing. That is the ability to get things done, to get results. Every

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: All these questions have one aim: to find out if the fellow is a man of action.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: As you study people—both the successful and the just average—you find they fall into two classes. The successful are active; we’ll call them activationists. The just average, the mediocre, the unsuccessful are passive. We’ll call them passivationists.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: A lot of passivationists got that way because they insisted on waiting until everything was 100 percent favorable before they took action. Perfection is highly desirable. But nothing man-made or man-designed is, or can be, absolutely perfect. So to wait for the perfect set of conditions is to wait forever.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Ideas are important. Let’s make no mistake about that. We must have ideas to create and improve anything. Success shuns the man who lacks ideas.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: That idea for getting more business, for simplifying work procedures, is of value only when it is acted upon.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: First, give your ideas value by acting on them. Regardless of how good the idea, unless you do something with it, you gain nothing.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Second, act on your ideas and gain mind tranquillity. Someone once said that the saddest words of tongue or pen are these: it might have been.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Action cures fear.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Build confidence. Destroy fear through action.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Action must precede action. That’s a law of nature. Nothing starts itself, not even the dozens of mechanical gadgets we use daily.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: A humorist once said the most difficult problem in life was getting out of a warm bed into a cold room. And he had a point. The longer you lie there and think how unpleasant it will be to get up, the more difficult it becomes.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: People who get things done in this world don’t wait for the spirit to move them; they move the spirit.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Do this today: Pick the one thing you like to do least. Then, without letting yourself deliberate on or dread the task, do it. That’s the most efficient way to handle chores.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 2. Next, use the mechanical way to create ideas, map out plans, solve problems, and do other work that requires top mental performance. Rather than wait for the spirit to move you, sit down and move your spirit.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: When you write a thought on paper, your full attention is automatically focused on that thought. That’s because the mind is not designed to think one thought and write another at the same time.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: When you want to think, start writing or doodling or diagramming. It’s an excellent way to move your spirit.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Take one example, saving money. Just about everybody agrees that saving money is a good idea. But just because it’s a good idea doesn’t mean many folks follow an organized savings and investment program. Many people have intentions to save, but only relatively few act on these intentions.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Business executives want comment. The fellow who hides his light under a bushel hurts himself. Get the “speak up” habit. Each time you speak up, you strengthen yourself. Come forward with your constructive ideas.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: But there’s a way to break this habit. Tell yourself, “I’m in condition right now to begin. I can’t gain a thing by putting it off. I’ll use the ‘get ready’ time and energy to get going instead.”

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: But like all progressive companies, we need new products, new markets, new and more efficient ways of doing things.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 1. Be a crusader. When you see something that you believe ought to be done, pick up the ball and run.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 2. Be a volunteer. Each of us has been in situations in which we wanted to volunteer for some activity but didn’t. Why? Because of fear.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: People place confidence in the fellow who acts. They naturally assume he knows what he is doing.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: GROW THE ACTION HABIT Practice these key points: 1. Be an activationist. Be someone who does things. Be a doer, not a don’t-er. 2. Don’t wait until conditions are perfect. They never will be. Expect future obstacles and difficulties and solve them as they arise. 3. Remember, ideas alone won’t bring success. Ideas have value only when you act upon them. 4. Use action to cure fear and gain confidence. Do what you fear, and fear disappears. Just try it and see. 5. Start your mental engine mechanically. Don’t wait for the spirit to move you. Take action, dig in, and you move the spirit. 6. Think in terms of now. Tomorrow, next week, later, and similar words often are synonymous with the failure word, never. Be an “I’m starting right now” kind of person. 7. Get down to business—pronto. Don’t waste time getting ready to act. Start acting instead. 8. Seize the initiative. Be a crusader. Pick up the ball and run. Be a volunteer. Show that you have the ability and ambition to do. Get in gear and go!

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: CAA officials, successful sales executives, physicians, football coaches, and professionals in every field follow this success principle: salvage something from every setback.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Decide right now to salvage something from every setback. Next time things seem to go wrong on the job or at home, calm down and find out what caused the trouble. This is the way to avoid making the same error twice.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Being self-critical is constructive. It helps you to build the personal strength and efficiency needed for success. Blaming others is destructive. You gain absolutely nothing from “proving” that someone else is wrong.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Persisting in one way is not a guarantee of victory. But persistence blended with experimentation does guarantee success.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Many ambitious people go through life with admirable persistence and show of ambition, but they fail to succeed because they don’t experiment with new approaches.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 1. Tell yourself, “There IS a way.” All thoughts are magnetic. As soon as you tell yourself, “I’m beaten. There’s no way to conquer this problem,” negative thoughts are attracted, and each of these helps convince you that you are right, that you are whipped.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: The difference between success and failure is found in one’s attitudes toward setbacks, handicaps, discouragements, and other disappointing situations.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 1. Study setbacks to pave your way to success. When you lose, learn, and then go on to win next time.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 2. Have the courage to be your own constructive critic. Seek out your faults and weaknesses and then correct them. This makes you a professional.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 3. Stop blaming luck. Research each setback. Find out what went wrong. Remember, blaming luck never got anyone where he wanted to go.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 4. Blend persistence with experimentation. Stay with your goal but don’t beat your head against a stone wall. Try new approaches. Experiment.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 5. Remember, there is a good side in every situation. Find it. See the good side and whip discouragement.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Goals are as essential to success as air is to life. No one ever stumbles into success without a goal. No one ever lives without air. Get a clear fix on where you want to go.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: The important thing is not where you were or where you are but where you want to get.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Before you start out, know where you want to go.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: No one accomplishes more than he sets out to accomplish. So visualize a big future.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: the most important qualification for an executive is the sheer desire to get ahead.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 1. Self-depreciation. You have heard dozens of people say, “I would like to be a doctor (or an executive or a commercial artist or in business for myself) but I can’t do it.” “I lack brains.” “I’d fail if I tried.” “I lack the education and/or experience.” Many young folks destroy desire with the old negative self-depreciation.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 2. “Security-itis.” Persons who say, “I’ve got security where I am” use the security weapons to murder their dreams.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 3. Competition. “The field is already overcrowded,” “People in that field are standing on top of each other” are remarks which kill desire fast.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 5. Family responsibility. The attitude of “It would have been wise for me to change over five years ago, but now I’ve got a family and I can’t change,” illustrates this kind of desire murder weapon.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: The person determined to achieve maximum success learns the principle that progress is made one step at a time.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: An hour is easy; forever is difficult.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Commit this question to memory and use it to evaluate everything you do: “Will this help take me where I want to go?” If the answer is no, back off; if yes, press ahead.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: There’s a lesson for each of us. To profit, to get the extra reward above a “normal” income in the years ahead, we must invest in ourselves. We must invest to achieve our goals.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 2. Invest in idea starters. Education helps you mold your mind, stretch it, train it to meet new situations and solve problems. Idea starters serve a related purpose. They feed your mind, give you constructive material to think about.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Achieving high-level success requires the support and the cooperation of others. And gaining this support and cooperation of others requires leadership ability. Success and the ability to lead others—that is, getting them to do things they wouldn’t do if they were not led—go hand in hand.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 4. Take time out to confer with yourself and develop your supreme thinking power.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: There are two special things you can do to develop your progressive outlook: 1. Think improvement in everything you do. 2. Think high standards in everything you do.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: What kind of world would this world be, If everyone in it were just like me? To add meaning to this self-imposed test, substitute the word company for world so it reads: What kind of company would this company be, If everyone in it were just like me?

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Am I a Progressive Thinker? Checklist A. Do I Think Progressively Toward My Work? 1. Do I appraise my work with the “how can we do it better?” attitude? 2. Do I praise my company, the people in it, and the products it sells at every possible opportunity? 3. Are my personal standards with reference to the quantity and quality of my output higher now than three or six months ago? 4. Am I setting an excellent example for my subordinates, associates, and others I work with?

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: The point is this: the successful person in any field takes time out to confer with himself or herself. Leaders use solitude to put the pieces of a problem together, to work out solutions, to plan, and, in one phrase, to do their superthinking.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Many people fail to tap their creative leadership power because they confer with everybody and everything else but themselves.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: As part of a professional development program I asked thirteen trainees to closet themselves for one hour each day for two weeks. The trainees were asked to shut themselves off from all distractions and think constructively about anything that came to mind. At the end of two weeks each trainee, without exception, reported the experience proved amazingly practical and worthwhile.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: when the fog is lifted, the right choice becomes crystal clear. Managed solitude pays off.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Perhaps early in the morning before anyone else is stirring about would be best for you. Or perhaps late in the evening would be a better time. The important thing is to select a time when your mind is fresh and when you can be free from distractions. You can use this time to do two types of thinking: directed and undirected. To do directed thinking, review the major problem facing you. In solitude your mind will study the problem objectively and lead you to the right answer.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Undirected thinking is very helpful in doing self-evaluation. It helps you get down to the very basic matters like “How can I do better? What should be my next move?”

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 1. Trade minds with the people you want to influence.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 2. Apply the “Be-Human” rule in your dealings with others. Ask, “What is the human way to handle this?”

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 3. Think progress, believe in progress, push for progress. Think improvement in everything you do. Think high standards in everything you do.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 4. Take time out to confer with yourself and tap your supreme thinking power. Managed solitude pays off. Use it to release your creative power.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: A. When Little People Try to Drive You Down, THINK BIG

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: B. When That “I-Haven’t-Got-What-It-Takes” Feeling Creeps Up on You, THINK BIG Remember: if you think you are weak, you are. If you think you’re inadequate, you are. If you think you’re second-class, you are.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 2. Concentrate on your assets. Build a sell-yourself-to-yourself commercial and use it. Learn to supercharge yourself. Know your positive self.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: 3. Put other people in proper perspective. The other person is just another human being, so why be afraid of him?

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: Think Big Enough to see that quarrels, arguments, feuds, and fusses will never help you get where you want to go.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: D. When You Feel Defeated, THINK BIG. It is not possible to achieve large success without hardships and setbacks.

Title: The Magic of Thinking Big
Author: David Joseph Schwartz
Highlight Text: F. When You Feel Your Progress on the Job Is Slowing Down, THINK BIG No matter what you do and regardless of your occupation, higher status, higher pay come from one thing: increasing the quality and quantity of your output. Do this: Think, “I can do better.” The best is not unattainable. There is room for doing everything better. Nothing in this world is being done as well as it could be. And when you think, “I can do better,” ways to do better will appear.

Title: The Martian: A Novel
Author: Andy Weir
Highlight Text: That’s all over now. I have no more jobs to do, and no more nature to defeat.

Title: The Master and Margarita
Author: Mikhail Bulgakov and Mirra Ginsburg
Highlight Text: “that every form of authority means coercion over men, and that a time will come when there shall be neither Caesars, nor any other rulers. Man will come into the kingdom of truth and justice, where there will be no need for any authority.”

Title: The Master Key System In Twenty-Four Parts With Questionnaire And Glossary, Unabridged Original Edition [Annotated]
Author: Charles F. Haanel
Highlight Text: we must “be” before we can “do,” and we can “ do “ only to the extent which we “are,” and what we “are” depends upon what we “think.”

Title: The Master Key System In Twenty-Four Parts With Questionnaire And Glossary, Unabridged Original Edition [Annotated]
Author: Charles F. Haanel
Highlight Text: We cannot express powers which we do not possess, and the only way to secure possession of power is to become conscious of power, and we can never become conscious of power until we learn that all power is from within.

Title: The Master Key System In Twenty-Four Parts With Questionnaire And Glossary, Unabridged Original Edition [Annotated]
Author: Charles F. Haanel
Highlight Text: The world without is a reflection of the world within. What appears without is what has been found within.

Title: The Master Key System In Twenty-Four Parts With Questionnaire And Glossary, Unabridged Original Edition [Annotated]
Author: Charles F. Haanel
Highlight Text: Mental efficiency is contingent upon harmony; discord means confusion; therefore, he who would acquire power must be in harmony with the law of his being.

Author: Charles F. Haanel
Highlight Text: It is therefore through the objective mind, or by wrong thinking, that we are related to all destructive forces.

Title: The Master Key System In Twenty-Four Parts With Questionnaire And Glossary, Unabridged Original Edition [Annotated]
Author: Charles F. Haanel
Highlight Text: All power is from within, and is absolutely under your control; it comes through exact knowledge and by the voluntary exercise of exact principles.

Title: The Master Key System In Twenty-Four Parts With Questionnaire And Glossary, Unabridged Original Edition [Annotated]
Author: Charles F. Haanel
Highlight Text: the great creative principle of the Universe; it is therefore creative and everything which you find in your world without has been created by you in the world within.

Highlight Text: Our biology expects activity—engagement of both our brains and our bodies with the people and world around us—as a signal to maintain health and function. Highlight Text: What exactly influences depth of field? Several factors come into play: the focal length of the lens, the distance between you and the subject you want to focus on, and the aperture you select. I feel strongly that of these three elements, aperture choice is the most important.

Title: Understanding Exposure, Fourth Edition: How to Shoot Great Photographs with Any Camera
Author: Bryan Peterson
Highlight Text: Optical law states that the smaller the opening of any lens (large f-stop numbers—16, 22, and 32), the greater the area of sharpness or detail in the photo. When you are using apertures at or near wide open (smaller f-stop numbers—2.8, 4, and 5.6), only the light that falls on the focused subject will be rendered as “sharp”; all the other light in the scene—the out-of-focus light—will “splatter” across the sensor or film. In effect, this unfocused light records as out-of-focus blobs, blurs, and blips.

Title: Understanding Exposure, Fourth Edition: How to Shoot Great Photographs with Any Camera
Author: Bryan Peterson
Highlight Text: When you wish to create a storytelling exposure, you will more often than not call upon your wide-angle lens, and when you combine it with small lens openings such as f/16 or f/22, you will record maximum depth of field. When you wish to isolate a subject from its “busy” surroundings, call upon the telephoto lenses: 100mm to 400mm. As a result of their much narrower front-to-back angle of view, you can often render all that “busyness” into out-of-focus tones and colors much more easily in combination with large lens openings such as f/5.6 or f/4.

This 1-meter setting applies only to the following: when using the focal lengths of 16–24mm on a full-frame camera (DX sensor) and when using the focal lengths of 10–16mm on a crop sensor camera (FX sensor).

Title: Your Move: The Underdog’s Guide to Building Your Business
Author: Ramit Sethi
Highlight Text: While many of my competitors use their words to harp on how many hours of HD video their courses include, and how much extra “stuff” you get when you purchase, I instead use my words to focus on the customer. What do they want? What are they frustrated with? What is going on inside their heads?
